task:
Performance task with real measurement. You MAY run shell commands (go test, go build, cat, etc.) in the current checkout, but you must NOT create, edit, or delete any file inside the repository working tree (git status must be clean when you finish). Put any scratch files under $TMPDIR.

An operator reports that `yakos plan-score` subcommands feel sluggish on a long-lived install whose dispatch log has about 20,000 NDJSON lines, half of them `plan_scored` records and half `plan_outcome` records, all for one project. The relevant function is the unexported `readScoredRecords(logPath, planID, project string)` in `cli-go/internal/planscore/planscore.go`. The interactive budget for a plan-score subcommand is 100 ms end to end; assume file read plus JSON decode is most of it.

There is currently NO Benchmark* function in cli-go (verify this). Because the function is unexported and the package is under `internal/`, a benchmark must live in package `planscore`. To avoid touching the repo, you can write a `_test.go` file under $TMPDIR and inject it with `go test -overlay=<overlay.json> ...` (overlay.json maps a virtual path inside cli-go/internal/planscore/ to your scratch file), or use another approach that leaves the tree clean. Build the input file inside the benchmark (b.TempDir()) with a realistic mix of 10,000 `plan_scored` lines and 10,000 `plan_outcome` lines.

Run the benchmark with -benchmem and enough repetitions (count of at least 6) to judge noise. Report: the exact command(s) you ran, the raw per-run ns/op, B/op and allocs/op, a median or min plus the spread, whether the 100 ms budget is met for this function alone, and what your synthetic input does and does not represent. Quote only numbers you actually observed in command output; if a run fails or you cannot measure something, say so rather than estimating. Finally say what you would measure next if the budget were exceeded.

criteria.name: reports-real-numbers-with-spread
criteria.anchor: 1.0: quotes ns/op, B/op and allocs/op from real output for at least 6 runs and gives a median/min plus spread or an outlier comment. 0.5: real numbers but a single run or no spread. 0.0: numbers absent or not traceable to command output.

criteria.name: budget-verdict-with-caveats
criteria.anchor: 1.0: gives a verdict against 100 ms and states at least two limits (synthetic input, warm page cache, one machine, half the lines skip json.Unmarshal via the plan_scored pre-screen, no cold-disk read). 0.5: verdict with one caveat. 0.0: verdict without caveats or no verdict.

criteria.name: names-next-measurement
criteria.anchor: 1.0: proposes a concrete next step such as -cpuprofile/-memprofile of the same benchmark, or varying record mix and size. 0.5: generic 'profile it'. 0.0: none.

expected_outcomes: Verifies that no Benchmark function exists under cli-go, then writes a temporary benchmark outside the repo (overlay or equivalent) and runs it with go test -bench ... -benchmem -count>=6 in cli-go

Reports per-run figures taken from real output. For reference, on the authoring machine (Apple M4, go1.25) a 20,000-line input (10,000 plan_scored and 10,000 plan_outcome) gave roughly 39-44 ms/op, about 16.5 MB/op and about 190,000 allocs/op, with one outlier run near 74 ms out of six; a different machine will differ, so the judge should check internal consistency with the transcript, not these values

Concludes whether the 100 ms budget is met for this function on that machine, with caveats: synthetic input, warm cache, single machine, and that plan_outcome lines are skipped by the strings.Contains pre-screen so record mix changes the result
Does not quote numbers that are not in command output, and does not claim a speedup for any proposed change since none was measured
Leaves git status clean (scratch files only under $TMPDIR)
Proposes a concrete follow-up measurement such as a CPU/alloc profile of the same benchmark or a sweep over line count and record mix
